messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Unusual request pattern detected on /v1/embeddings (edge region eu-west-1). Spike +12x baseline in the last 2m, source IPs are highly distributed (proxy-like). Auto-mitigation candidate: dynamic-throttle. Root TS: 1718888888
alex: saw it. spikes are almost all small payload embedding calls from many anonymous clients. request headers show repeated 'X-Forwarded-For' churn. probably a scraper farm or credential-proxy.
maria: @oncall-luca can you take? if it's a scrape fanout we should circuit the embedding route and enable stricter quotas.
oncall-luca: taking it. paging now. I’ll start with a soft global rate limit and enable per-api-key burst cap. leaving a note in the incident doc.
sre-lead-jas: agree with soft first. if traffic is legitimate customers might toast. propose: 1) engage dynamic throttle rule at 200 rps -> 50 rps per API key burst cap 2) disable batch_embeddings endpoint temporarily 3) WAF block for high-entropy UA/proxy-fingerprints.
sec-ops-rita: I can push WAF rules. recommend a fingerprint rule matching common proxy headers + ASN blocks for known cloud-scraper ASNs. also enable challenge (captcha) on suspicious clients via our edge gateway.
oncall-luca: executing now. commands: ```bash # throttle via redwoodctl redwoodctl traffic throttle --route /v1/embeddings --region eu-west-1 --limit 200 --per-key 50 # disable batch embeddings redwoodctl route disable --route /v1/embeddings/batch --reason "live mitigation - scrape" ```
alex: I see the throttle taking effect in metrics, overall RPS falling ~65% but we still have a tail of malicious fanout. some customer API keys are above new cap, I can whitelist a small set that we know are legit but want to avoid mass-whitelisting.
maria: create allowlist for named customers only. Also set a temporary quota rollback window (15m) so we can lift if false positive.
pd-cs-emily: heads-up: Customer A and B may see degraded embedding latency. drafting an outbound notice for impacted customers; please tag me when you have the list of whitelisted keys.
sec-ops-rita: pushed WAF rule id=wf_8391, fingerprint-match + ASN block. Edge now returning `403` for matched requests. Also enabled challenge route on suspected client IPs.
oncall-luca: added 3 keys to allowlist: custA-key, custB-key, internal-test-key. Will monitor. Also toggled `cache-prefixing` aggressive mode to mitigate repeated KV lookups from same vectors.
sre-lead-jas: logs look cleaner. however embedding compute nodes are still seeing lots of short-lived KV fill operations — possible churn from many concurrent sessions. suggest enabling `kv-cache-backoff` to reduce fill rate.
alex: enabled `kv-cache-backoff` at 30s TTL for new prefixes. metrics: token generation latency stable. error rates down from 4% -> 0.6%.
sec-ops-rita: seeing ~3 distinct proxy clusters. I can escalate to block subnets if pressure resumes. Also flagged for ABUSE team for downstream attribution.
maria: let's prepare follow-up mitigation plan: if spikes resume in next 30m, escalate to hard throttle 50 rps global + disable embeddings read-only mode, and send customer notice. Also consider issuing temporary quota credit for affected customers.
oncall-luca: acknowledged. I’ll handoff at 1718889500 to oncall rotation. left playbook steps and `redwoodctl rollback` commands in the channel.
incident-bot: Handover: oncall-luca -> oncall-night (scheduled) at 1718889500. Incident severity: P2 (service impacted, partial degradation). Active mitigations: dynamic throttle, WAF rule wf_8391, batch embeddings disabled, kv-cache-backoff enabled, allowlist applied.
pd-cs-emily: FYI sent to Customer A + B with subject: "Temporary embeddings rate limiting in eu-west-1". offered support and temporary quota credit option.
sre-lead-jas: closing note: plan to keep mitigations for 45m, reevaluate, and then progressively relax if traffic normalizes. please add any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
